REGARDING
PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
Fundamentally, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize community welfare. Therefore, in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining national unity, cohesion and harmony, improving the quality of life of the community and realizing justice and equity.
The unequal distribution of opportunities in all areas of life, including in the fields of education and employment, can give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in Karanganyar Regency there are still acts of violence both physical, psychological, sexual, neglect of women in the household and even human trafficking, and this constitutes a violation of human rights.
Acts of violence and neglect are fundamentally violations of Human Rights. Therefore, to provide a sense of security, fulfillment of rights and recovery of victims, there needs to be Protection efforts for women.
Protection carried out by the Government towards women is concretely implemented, namely through the issuance of Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), hereinafter abbreviated as CEDAW.
The government's efforts in protecting its citizens, especially women, are also clearly implied in the provisions of Article 3 paragraph (2) of Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights which states that: "every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, Protection and fair legal treatment as well as obtaining legal certainty and equal treatment before the law".
Violence and trafficking against women have been regulated in Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2003 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Human Trafficking. Therefore, it is the obligation of the Regional Government to protect, prevent and take action against violations of Violence against Women through its regulation in Regional Regulations, so that the community respects and honors the rights of women as they respect human rights.
In this Regional Regulation, the responsibilities and obligations of the Regional Government in the Protection of women are regulated, starting from prevention, Protection services, to the recovery of women victims of various acts of violence, so that with this Regional Regulation it is hoped that various acts of Violence against Women will no longer exist in Karanganyar Regency.

5.8.rationale: The Indonesian regulation does explicitly engage private-sector actors through employment provisions: Pasal 11–12 regulate employers ("Pengusaha") and require them to provide protection for female workers (Pasal 12(1): "Pengusaha ... wajib memberikan Perlindungan"). This is direct private-sector involvement. Although the retrieved candidates shown to the judge did not include the actual text of Pasal 11–12 (only a heading “Employment Protection”), the candidate set did include Pasal 29 huruf i: "memberikan Perlindungan bagi pekerja/buruh perempuan" and the definition of P2TP2A listing "pusat konsultasi usaha" (business consultation center), both of which point toward engagement beyond government/community alone. A careful judge could have inferred private-sector relevance from the employer obligations in the policy area, but the judge required explicit mention in the provided snippets and answered No. Overall, the policy supports a Yes for private-sector engagement; the model’s decision was too strict given the policy’s employer-focused provisions.
